Native source ownership: fortress/adventure ended-game panel

Actual images are resolved from data/runtime/native-pe-images.json.
Steam: D:/program/steam/steamapps/common/Dwarf Fortress/Dwarf Fortress.exe
Classic: C:/Users/WIN11/Downloads/df_53_16_win/Dwarf Fortress.exe
Both are Windows x64 PE images. native-functions.tsv retains their PE identity.
The *-ghidra.c files are actual Ghidra 12.1.4 decompiler output. The matching
*.asm files retain the input instructions. end-state-branches.tsv joins native
title/body literal references with the real mode/state branch destinations.
Ghidra recovers switches from the actual comparison bounds and table data;
no manual BasicOverride is installed. native-switches.tsv additionally retains
the actual ordered jump-table entries, including shared destinations. Modes 9
and 10 remain separate case labels leading into their shared native branch.

State ownership (offsets from the Escape-menu state):
  +0x04: constructor mode
  +0x08: std::string title
  +0x28: std::vector<std::string *> paragraph lines
  +0x48: action IDs
  +0x60: action parameters

Ended-state constructor:
  Steam RVA 0x1e65a0; classic RVA 0x1e6530.
  Mode 1 dispatches on the fortress ending WORD at Steam RVA 0x2391230.
    3: Abandoned / Your settlement has been abandoned.
    2: Retired / Your fortress has settled into the rhythm of day-to-day
       living, beyond your meticulous concern.
    1: Conquered / Your strength has been broken.
    0 and all other values: Withered / Your settlement has crumbled to its end.
  Mode 9: Retired / You settle in this location...
  Mode 10: Dead / Your adventure has come to an end.
  Modes 9 and 10 share the mode-switch destination, then compare mode against 9.
  All six choices append action ID 10 and its -1 parameter.
  That action is Save world and return to title menu.

Paragraph production:
  Native width is 0x3a (58 columns).
  Single-string wrapper Steam RVA 0x8e7310 / classic RVA 0x8e4b80 creates
  a one-element vector and calls the line wrapper Steam RVA 0x8e7440 /
  classic RVA 0x8e4cb0. The Conquered branch calls the line wrapper directly;
  the Dead branch inlines the equivalent line-building operation.
  These strings are the complete authored sentences, not individual words.
  Inline SIMD/QWORD copies in Ghidra are rejoined by native-literals.tsv using
  their actual .rdata roots, including all 95 characters of the retired text.

Paragraph drawing:
  Full renderer Steam RVA 0x1ddd50 / classic RVA 0x1ddce0.
  Title: addst call 0x1e1934 / 0x1e18c4; return 0x1e1939 / 0x1e18c9.
  One paragraph line: addst call 0x1e19b1 / 0x1e1941;
    return 0x1e19b6 / 0x1e1946; horizontally centered.
  Multiple lines: addst call 0x1e1a53 / 0x1e19e3;
    return 0x1e1a58 / 0x1e19e8; common x = panel left + 2, y increments by 1.
  Native addst Steam RVA 0xad9960 / classic RVA 0xad69a0 draws the stored line.
  This panel does not draw its paragraph through curses_textbox. The complete
  paragraph must be matched before ordinary short literal substitutions.

Shared actions/save path/music:
  native-pause-sources.tsv retains the full renderer, mode constructor,
  input dispatch, save update, save action, metadata readers and native tables.
  All sixteen action choices and every native save-stage string are retained.
  The ended-game path uses ID 10 and subsequently mode 4 (fortress) or mode 8
  (adventure); save destination choices and progress belong to those shared
  renderer branches, not additional ended-game body variants.
  The lower music panel belongs to the same renderer. Its five status prefixes
  are Track playing:, Last track:, Interlude playing:, Last interlude:, and
  Combat music:. Full native music selector tables and finite TITLE/AUTHOR
  values are retained in native-pause-sources.tsv; arbitrary MUSIC_FILE TITLE
  and AUTHOR metadata are read through the map fallback (+0x10 and +0x30).
  TITLE/AUTHOR values are authored soundtrack metadata, not missing UI prose.

Reproduction tools:
  tools/extract_fortress_game_over_sources.py reads the configured images with
  the fixed native objdump and retains branch literals/addresses/instructions.
  tools/DecompileFortressGameOver.java consumes those files with headless
  Ghidra to decompile the same PE images. Neither tool executes the game,
  generates translation runtime data, compiles the mod, or controls a window.
